Home/Registry
Catalogue · registry

Registry of open 3D-printable robots.

309 publicly available robotics projects with printed parts. In most of them printing makes up a substantial part of the build, in some only a smaller part; each lists its printed share where we know it. The catalogue picks the ones we have renders and detailed pages for; the registry is the full list.

← Back to the robot catalogue

What you may do with prints

Six rights classes

The label on each project follows the hardware licence, i.e. the printed parts and CAD files. Software and documentation may be under a different licence; each project lists the exact wording.

Permissive
You may print, modify and sell the parts. Usually you have to credit the author and the licence (e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0, CC BY, CERN-OHL-P).
Copyleft
You may print, modify and sell. When you distribute or sell modified parts or files, you have to publish their sources under the same licence and credit the author (e.g. CC BY-SA, GPL, CERN-OHL-S/W).
Non-commercial only
Printing and modifying for yourself, a school or a club. Selling prints or kits needs the author’s permission (e.g. CC BY-NC).
No modifications
You may share the files only as they are. Don’t publish modified versions without the author’s permission (e.g. CC BY-ND).
Closed
The author reserves the rights. Sharing the files (even unmodified), printing for others, publishing modifications or selling prints needs their permission.
Licence not confirmed
The project states no licence, or it states one that we have not been able to confirm (for example for files on Thingiverse or Printables). Until you have checked the licence on the project, assume the author keeps all rights: sharing the files (even unmodified), printing for others, publishing modifications or selling prints needs their permission.

This is a simplified overview; the full licence text on the project is what counts. More in the guide Open-source hardware licences explained.

Some projects have strong motors, sharp parts or lithium batteries, and the lab projects handle liquids and biological material. Younger builders should work with an adult. The “school” rating assumes work under a teacher’s supervision.

309 projects

The projects

Data come from the projects’ repositories, licence files and papers. Licences and links were checked on 2026-11-07; other details may be incomplete, and what we could not verify is marked “not stated”. The fit for makers and schools is our estimate on a 1–5 scale. There are no project images here; you’ll find them behind the source links.

What’s missing

Gaps

Standard equipment for which our research on 1 November 2026 found no open design with a substantial 3D-printed share. This includes types where the licence or the files could not be verified.

Biology
heat block / dry bath, water bath, incubator (as a standalone device), CO2 incubator, laminar flow / clean bench, sterilisers / autoclaves, micromanipulator, colony counter (hardware), plate reader, transilluminator / gel imager, plate handler / microplate tools
Chemistry
stirring hotplate, overhead stirrer, pH meter, conductivity meter, melting point apparatus, thermostatted bath, lab stands / clamps / holders, electrospinning
Physics
polarimeter, linear / translation stages, air track, dynamics carts / inclined plane, ripple tank / waves, sound / Kundt tube / resonance, cloud chamber, electrostatics (Van de Graaff, Wimshurst), laser safety enclosures, vacuum chamber parts
Agriculture
field robot platform / row-crop rover, weeding robot, mechanical, weeding, laser, harvesting robot / fruit gripper, soil sampling / probes, livestock: feeding / feed pushers, livestock monitoring (collars, etc.), pollination robots, agricultural drones (printed frames), beehive monitoring / bee counters, insect / pest monitoring, mushroom fruiting chambers, insect farming (mealworms, black soldier fly), seed counting / sorting, open tractors, plant gravitropism / clinostats
Desktop
polargraph / vertical plotter, air-hockey / game robots, desktop robot arm with conveyor (Dobot-like workcell)
